key_insight: A-site high-entropy disorder and tensile strain jointly improve oxygen evolution activity in nickelate thin films, while the high-entropy composition enhances structural stability relative to LaNiO3.
engineering_relevance: This work offers a materials-design route for perovskite oxide water-splitting electrocatalysts, rather than solar cells or AI systems.
method: Study epitaxial (La0.2Pr0.2Nd0.2Sm0.2Eu0.2)NiO3 films under different strain conditions.
Probe structural defects, Ni valence, and electronic states using spectroscopy and structural characterization.
Combine first-principles calculations with OER activity and degradation comparisons.
evidence_signal: Tensile-strained films exhibit earlier OER onset, stronger pre-catalytic Ni redox features, and higher activity than compressively strained films and representative single-A-site nickelates; the high-entropy nickelate also resists structural degradation better than LaNiO3.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative activity or durability metrics, and transfer from epitaxial thin films to practical electrodes remains unestablished.
paper_title: High-Entropy A-Site Disorder Enhances Oxygen Evolution Reaction Activity and Stability in Nickelate Thin Films
